scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: A helicopter can hover in one spot, fly backwards and land almost anywhere. How does it do that without wings?

scenes.name: rotor
scenes.text: It does have wings. The rotor blades are long, thin wings that spin, pushing air down to create lift.

scenes.name: collective
scenes.text: Tilting all blades to a steeper angle together makes more lift to climb. Flattening them lets it descend.

scenes.name: cyclic
scenes.text: The pilot can also tilt the whole spinning disc. Tilt it forward, and the helicopter flies forward.

scenes.name: tail
scenes.text: Spinning the main rotor tries to spin the body the other way. The tail rotor pushes sideways to stop that.

scenes.name: pedals
scenes.text: Foot pedals change the tail rotor's push, letting the pilot turn the nose left or right.

scenes.name: hard
scenes.text: All these controls affect each other, which is why helicopters are known as tricky to fly.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Spinning wings, a tilting disc, a tail rotor. Follow for more on how things really work.
